200.title: ‘Single State’: Polish politician claims Ukraine tried to drag Poland into war with Russia
200.body: ‘Single State’: Polish politician claims Ukraine tried to drag Poland into war with Russia Jens Asbjørn Bøgen • Follow dagens.com on Google Shutterstock.com “During the early months of the war, Zelenskyy tried to get Poland to enter the conflict, possibly by creating a single state, Polish opposition leader Jarosław Kaczyński claimed.” Others are reading now Terrified Russians flee Putin’s war: “They have seen what happened” Israel vs. A Simple Explainer Speaking at a youth forum in Augustów, the leader of the Polish opposition party Law and Justice Jarosław Kaczyński reflected on the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and during the speech, he claimed Ukrainian officials initially urged Warsaw to take steps Poland could not accept. He alleged that Ukrainian leaders wanted to draw Poland directly into the war, even by forming a single state.

200.title: NATO fighter jets scrambled as Poland and Latvia issue air alerts during Russian attack on Ukraine
200.summary: NATO fighter jets were scrambled in eastern Europe as Poland and Latvia raised airspace alerts during a major Russian aerial attack on Ukraine. An emergency RCB alert was sent to residents across 24 districts of Poland’s Lublin Voivodeship, warning that a Russian air attack was underway in Ukraine and that Polish military aircraft were operating in national airspace.
200.body: NATO fighter jets were scrambled in eastern Europe as Poland and Latvia raised airspace alerts during a major Russian aerial attack on Ukraine. An emergency RCB alert was sent to residents across 24 districts of Poland’s Lublin Voivodeship, warning that a Russian air attack was underway in Ukraine and that Polish military aircraft were operating in national airspace. Separately, NATO Baltic Air Policing fighter jets were scrambled over Latvia after authorities detected a possible threat to the country’s airspace in the Krāslava municipality near Belarus. Neither Poland nor Latvia reported a confirmed violation of their airspace during the alerts.

400.title: Crédit Agricole CIB gets €2.4 billion in investment in European energy grids
400.summary: Crédit Agricole CIB gets €2.4 billion in investment in European energy grids The EIB will provide up to €300 million in counter-guarantees, enabling Crédit Agricole CIB to commit an equivalent amount and build a portfolio of bank guarantees worth up to €600 million.
400.body: Crédit Agricole CIB gets €2.4 billion in investment in European energy grids The EIB will provide up to €300 million in counter-guarantees, enabling Crédit Agricole CIB to commit an equivalent amount and build a portfolio of bank guarantees worth up to €600 million. A new agreement between the European Investment Bank (EIB) and Crédit Agricole CIB is expected to mobilise up to €2.4 billion in investment in energy grids across the European Union, supporting infrastructure development, industrial competitiveness and security of supply. A Broader European Push for Energy Infrastructure The operation forms part of the EIB's €1.5 billion Energy Grids Package, announced in 2025 to support the development, modernisation and reinforcement of networks across the EU.

500.title: Enterprise AI Doesn’t Need Better Models But Better Workflows
500.summary: Enterprise AI Doesn’t Need Better Models But Better Workflows Think your business is saving millions on AI? The question is whether you have moved from optimising token costs to optimising the cost of an accepted business outcome; and whether you have built a process in which AI can actually make that outcome cheaper .
500.body: Enterprise AI Doesn’t Need Better Models But Better Workflows Think your business is saving millions on AI? Where AI reduces the cost of an outcome The cost of an accepted outcome is lowest where two conditions overlap: complex, unstructured inputs and an output that a human can verify within seconds . Processes win, not models Our cases demonstrate one thing: the cost of an outcome falls not when a newer model appears, but when the process around it is redesigned. The question is whether you have moved from optimising token costs to optimising the cost of an accepted business outcome; and whether you have built a process in which AI can actually make that outcome cheaper .
